title: Abstract skeleton: headings, word budget, what each section must establish
outcome: A skeleton Aarav fills in himself: problem -> fix -> why it matters, with a word budget and the points each section must land
acceptance: Section headings in the organisers' order (problem -> fix -> why it matters, plus limits) with a word budget per section totalling 850-950, under the 1,000 cap
Under each heading: bullet notes (fragments, max ~12 words each) of what must be established, each tagged to a fact-card row, guardrail or term; zero full sentences of abstract prose (Charter)
Reflects D1 layered headline, D2 METR wording, D3 one credited Airlock clause, D12 hero scenario, D13 numbers-as-targets
summary:
v2 after panel changes. abstract/SKELETON.md: every point bullet tagged MUST/IF-ROOM (55 MUSTs, cap 60 at ~1 per 15 words; per-subsection counts in the budget table); rules and ✗ lists moved to untagged Guard: lines. Panel's demotions applied; Airlock #7 numbers deleted; TTI/TTC defined once in 3b; binding rule: section totals binding, subsections ±15, bullet order free.
Reframe: 1a (100) opens on the brief's 'without discarding' clause, shown with the IBAN example (moved from 2a) -> honest work built on the bad write -> 'undo crm' undefined [P1]. 2a deleted; 2b walks the example. Budgets 1a 100 / 1b 90 / 1c 110 / 2b 80 / 2c 45 / 2d 65 / 2e 95 / 2f 45; totals 300 / 330 / 900. Scores: lines map 2c/2d/2e to time-to-identify / time-to-contain / clean recovery.
Should-fix + nits: 3a tags 'audited, not only demoed' [CHARTER]; 3b RES-08 headline bullet ('in the standards we checked'); 1b '✗ internal / cyber [#1]', stale P2 flag dropped; 2d 'reconciliation mismatch (class U)'; 3c NIST MANAGE 4.3 -> RES-08 [19].
GUARDRAILS v3: F11 'approved' recovery-plan step; W4 cites RES-08 [19] for NIST MANAGE 4.3; new W7 (brief's scores lack an agreed measurement in the standards we checked; we define checkable ones; RES-08). Changes v2 (SKELETON) / v3 (GUARDRAILS) notes added.
review:
[panel · changes] CHANGES: 2 must-fix, both cheap. Structure passes. The order is problem -> fix -> why -> limits; budgets total 900 and every subsection sums correctly. D1 is layered as decided (gap 1a, provenance 2b, selective undo 2e only, testimony vs evidence 3a, flagged for Aarav). D2: 1b uses card #1/#2 qualifiers and the never-quote items. D3: the box gives one credited clause, P5's journal point goes inside it or unnamed, and the 'dense spread' fix is carried. D12: F2+ with the W6 label and x10 kept out of the story. D13: definitions + targets, no seconds. Cross-checks against FACT-CARD, GUARDRAILS v2, TERMS and C6 v2 are clean: 'never cancelled here' in 2d vs cancel_outbox in 2e is correct.\nPASTEABLE-PROSE CHECK: PASS. No bullet is a sentence. The quoted strings ('tamper-evident up to the last witnessed head', 'orthogonal rollback', 'maps to', 'in a safe state') are mandated wording or attributed quotations, not prose. The writing-plan sentences are instructions. The residual risk is structural: ~124 bullets in a fixed order invite one sentence per bullet, which reads kit-shaped and machine-like. Must-fix 1 also addresses that.\nMUST-FIX 1: the budget cannot hold the points. 1c has 12 bullets plus a 7-bullet box in 120 words, and the clause alone is 20-30. 2d has 10 in 60, 2e has 12 in 75, 2f has 7 in 40. Every line reads as 'must establish', so Aarav either overruns or writes telegraphic text, and both hurt with this jury. Tag every bullet MUST or IF-ROOM, at most ~1 MUST per 15 budget words. Demote these to IF-ROOM: 1b #9 catalogued incidents (keep 'single-agent, in our search' only as a qualifier) and #3 hindsight; 1c sagas #13, OTel #11, FAMAS #6, random baseline #5; the box's optional #7 numbers (delete them: they cannot fit in 30 words beside 'by design', 'orthogonal rollback', 'complementary' and the arXiv ID); 2b MCP #12; 2d epoch and anti-framing; 2e append-only, over-taint (L2 covers it) and the dry-run chain (keep 'approved plan'); 2f tamper-alert freeze. Define TTI/TTC once, in 3b: delete the duplicates in 2c/2d. Add one line under the budget table: section totals are binding; subsections are +/-15 and bullet order inside a subsection is free. ABS-07 reviewers then enforce totals, not micro-budgets.\nMUST-FIX 2: the framing can be sharper. The jury 'rewards the team that frames the problem best'. Our strongest frame is that the brief's own requirement ('reverses one agent's damage WITHOUT discarding the other agents' work') is undefined once honest agents have read the bad write. 1a states that abstractly, and the IBAN example only arrives in 2a, inside the fix. Move the example into 1a so the gap is shown, not told. 1a bullets: brief's frame + brief's 'without discarding' clause [CHARTER] -> crm swaps IBAN; billing/payments/comms acted on it; inventory/docs untouched [D12 · W6 label] -> their work is honest AND built on the bad write -> 'undo crm' undefined [P1]. Rebudget: 1a 70->100, 1b 110->90, 1c 120->110 (problem stays 300). Delete 2a: 2b opens by walking the example. Then 2b 70->80, 2d 60->65, 2e 75->95, 2f 40->45 (fix stays 330, total 900). Also show in 2c/2d/2e that they map 1:1 to the brief's three scores (time-to-identify / time-to-contain / clean recovery). That is already the structure; one tag line per heading makes it explicit.\nSHOULD-FIX: 3a, tag the brief's 'an agent that can be audited, not only demoed' [CHARTER]; testimony vs evidence answers it directly. 3b, add a bullet: the brief's three scores have no agreed measurement in the standards we checked -> we define checkable ones, scored against the oracle [RES-08 headline; qualifier 'in the standards we checked']. Ask zoya to add it to GUARDRAILS as W7 if adopted.\nNits: 1b, '✗ internal / cyber [#1]' is enough; the 'card #1 overrides P2' flag is stale because P2 is fixed in ABS-02 v2. 2d, write 'reconciliation mismatch (class U)', not bare 'class U' (D7). 3c, NIST MANAGE 4.3 is sourced in RES-08 [19], not on the card; tag it there. Re-review is quick once the tags and the 1a move are in.

[panel · done] DONE. v2 resolves both must-fixes, and the should-fixes and nits are in.
MUST-FIX 1 (budget vs points): PASS. Every point bullet is tagged. 55 MUST and 33 IF-ROOM. I counted MUSTs per subsection and they match the table: 1a 6, 1b 6, 1c 3 + box 4, 2b 5, 2c 3, 2d 4, 2e 6, 2f 3, 3a 4, 3b 4, 3c 2, Limits 3, Show 2. No subsection goes above about 1 MUST per 15 budget words. All the demotions I listed are applied. The #7 numbers and their 'dense spread' line are gone, and a Guard bars them from the clause. TTI/TTC is defined only in 3b, and 2c/2d point there. The binding rule sits under the table: section totals binding, subsections ±15, bullet order free. Guard: lines carry no tag and cost no words, which is the right split.
MUST-FIX 2 (framing): PASS. 1a opens on the brief's 'without discarding' clause, which matches CHARTER line 10. It then shows the gap with the IBAN example: crm swaps, billing/payments/comms act on it, inventory/docs untouched, their work is honest AND built on the bad write, so 'undo crm' is undefined [P1]. The ×10 Guard moved with it. 2a is deleted and 2b opens by walking the example. Budgets: 1a 100, 1b 90, 1c 110, 2b 80, 2c 45, 2d 65, 2e 95, 2f 45. Totals 300 / 330 / 170 / 85 = 900 plus the 15-word title. Scores: lines tie 2c/2d/2e 1:1 to time-to-identify / time-to-contain / clean recovery.
SHOULD-FIX + NITS: PASS. 3a quotes 'audited, not only demoed' verbatim (CHARTER line 14). The 3b W7 bullet keeps 'in the standards we checked', and GUARDRAILS v3 W7 matches it. F11 has the 'approved' recovery-plan step and agrees with 2d ('never cancelled here') and 2e (cancel as an approved plan step). 1b now reads '✗ internal / cyber [#1]'. 2d now reads 'reconciliation mismatch (class U)'. 3c tags NIST to RES-08 [19].
PASTEABLE-PROSE CHECK: PASS again. Every bullet is a fragment of arrows, colons and middots. The only full sentences are the key, the binding rule, the writing plan and the Changes notes, and all of those are instructions. Writing-plan step 5 still requires own words typed in an editor, nothing pasted. Fewer MUSTs also removes the one-sentence-per-bullet risk I raised in v1.
Optional nits (no re-review): (a) some bullets run 13-17 tokens counting symbols (3b TTI line, W7 bullet, 2e triage). About 12 real words, fine as notes. (b) Section 2 now starts at 2b. Keep the labels, since ABS-07 comments and this log cite them, or add '(2a merged into 1a)' beside the heading. (c) 1b is the densest section (6 MUSTs, mostly qualifiers, in 90 words). Tell Aarav the qualifiers can be a parenthetical, not separate clauses.
